svg.title: When African countries became independent
svg.desc: Map of Africa coloured by period of independence: before 1950 (Liberia, Ethiopia, Egypt and South Africa); the 1950s (Libya, Sudan, Morocco, Tunisia, Ghana and Guinea); 1960 to 1964, when most countries gained independence; 1965 to 1969; the 1970s (the Portuguese colonies and Djibouti); and 1980 or later (Zimbabwe 1980, Namibia 1990, Eritrea 1993 and South Sudan 2011). Western Sahara remains disputed.
svg.text: 1960 alone saw seventeen African countries become independent.
